# Service Reminder Automation

Hi Kira,

I want to start by apologising for how long this has taken. This one genuinely caught me out — a platform integration we had planned to use at the centre of this solution was retired by the vendor, right as we were finalising the approach. Rather than rush you something that would have broken six months in, I went back to the drawing board. The upside is we now have a much clearer picture of what is actually available and what will stand the test of time. I'm trying to go for something that doesn't have huge ongoing costs and is not overly technical. I'd like something that you can manage easily.
* * *

## The problem in plain terms

Right now you spend time each week manually:

*   Searching Xero for motors installed around two years ago
*   Checking Google Calendar to confirm no recent service visit has happened
*   Checking whether the property is real estate-managed (so the reminder goes to the agent, not the owner)
*   Sending the right email template based on the motor type

The goal is to automate as much of this as possible so it runs quietly in the background each week without you needing to touch it.
* * *

## What we looked at

We reviewed a number of options including ServiceM8, which is widely used in the trades — in fact my own electrician and gas guys both run on it. It is a solid platform and worth knowing about, but it has one significant limitation for your use case: its service reminder feature maxes out at 12 months. For a two-year reminder cycle it simply cannot do it without a clunky workaround, so we ruled it out for this.

We also reviewed HubSpot (the integration that was retired), Zoho, and several automation platforms before landing on the three options below.
* * *

## The options

### Option A — FieldPulse

_Best fit if you have an appetite for a shift in how you manage your jobs day-to-day_

FieldPulse is software built specifically for trades businesses. When you install a motor, you record it as an asset in FieldPulse - make, model, installation date. The system then tracks that asset and automatically triggers a service reminder at the two-year mark, no searching required. It syncs two-ways with Xero so your customer and financial data stays connected.

The honest trade-off: this means running your jobs through FieldPulse going forward — scheduling, quoting, and service history all in one place. That is a big change to how you work, and it's obviously not something to take on lightly. But if you have ever thought about shifting to one platfrom across the whole business, this solves the reminder problem as a natural part of doing that, rather than as a bolt-on.

We would recommend getting a demo before committing to anything (of course!).

_Estimated ongoing cost: to be confirmed based on your job volume:_
[https://www.fieldpulse.com/](https://www.fieldpulse.com/)
* * *

### Option B — [Make.com](http://Make.com) automation

_Our recommendation if you want to keep your current tools and just fix the reminder problem_

This option keeps everything you already use - Xero, Gmail, and Google Calendar and adds an automation layer on top that runs a weekly check in the background.

Because we want you to be confident in it before it starts sending emails on your behalf, we would build this in two phases:

**Phase 1 — You stay in the loop**
The automation runs each week, finds who is due for a reminder, checks your calendar for recent visits, and prepares a ready-to-review list with draft emails for each contact. You review it, make any tweaks, and approve the send. You stay in control while we prove the system is working correctly.

**Phase 2 — Fully hands-off**
Once you are confident it is getting it right, we switch it to send automatically. From that point it runs without you needing to do anything.

[Make.com](http://Make.com) is visual and relatively straightforward to work with once it is set up. There is a good chance we could hand the day-to-day maintenance over to you down the track if you wanted that.

**The drawbacks to be aware of:**

*   If the logic needs to change significantly (new motor types, different reminder rules), we would need to go back in and rebuild parts of it
*   [Make.com](http://Make.com) charges based on the number of operations it runs each month — at your current volume this is comfortably within the lowest plan, but it is worth knowing the model
*   It is dependent on [Make.com](http://Make.com) as a platform, though they are well established

_Estimated ongoing cost: ~$14/month AUD_
[https://www.make.com/en/pricing](https://www.make.com/en/pricing)
* * *

### Option C — n8n

_More powerful under the hood, but more technical_

Same concept as Option B - keeps your existing tools, automates the weekly check - but built on a platform called n8n. Both [Make.com](http://Make.com) and n8n require us to set them up, but where [Make.com](http://Make.com) is visual and something we could eventually hand to you to maintain, n8n is a more technical platform. It is very powerful and flexible if your needs change over time, but any modifications would need to come back through us. Good if you want a pure set-and-forget system and are not interested in ever touching it yourself.

_Estimated ongoing cost: ~$37/month AUD_
[https://n8n.io/pricing/](https://n8n.io/pricing/)
* * *

## Things that need to be true for any of this to work

Regardless of which option you go with, a few things need to be in order first. None of these are blockers, but I want to be upfront about them:

1. **Xero invoices need to distinguish installs from service calls** — the automation needs to know which invoice marks the original installation (to start the two-year clock). If your invoice types are already coded differently in Xero, great. If not, it is a quick tidy-up.
2. **Product codes need to be present and consistent on invoices** — the right email template is selected based on the product code. Worth a quick check that these are reliably on your Xero invoices.
3. **Google Calendar event naming needs to be consistent** _(Options B and C only)_ — the system checks your Google Calendar to see if a customer has had a recent service visit. For this to work reliably, appointments need to be named consistently — for example, always including the customer name or property address in the event title. If the naming varies, the system can miss a recent visit and send a reminder to someone you have just been to. This is something you would need to commit to going forward.
4. **Real estate contacts need to be flagged** — the system needs to know which contacts are real estate-managed so it can route reminders to the agent rather than the owner. The simplest way is a contact group or tag in Xero, which you mentioned you were already open to setting up.
* * *

## Our recommendation

If you want to keep your current setup and solve just the reminder problem: **Option B (**[**Make.com**](http://Make.com)**)** is the right starting point. Low ongoing cost, no platform change, and Phase 1 keeps you in control while we get it dialled in.

If you have been thinking about getting more structured across the whole business — job management, asset tracking, service history in one place: **Option A (FieldPulse)** is worth a proper look. It is a bigger commitment, but the reminder automation is built in rather than bolted on.
* * *

## Where are you at?

Before we go any further I would love to know where your head is at — does one of these directions feel right, or are there questions you want to work through first? Happy to jump on a call if that is easier.

Have a read through the options and let me know your thoughts — once you have a direction in mind I can give you a proper idea of costs.

Raels
